newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UNHCR slams Germany's Bosnia refugee repatriations.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR slams Germany's Bosnia refugee repatriations.

text.p: A U.N. refugee agency on Friday criticised Germany's forced repatriation of Bosnian refugees as premature because many of those affected were still barred from their homes by nationalist hardliners.
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said it had learned that Germany planned to deport a group of about 70 Bosnians on Saturday and 100 more a week later.
A significant number of them are Moslems or Croats who fled Serb-controlled territory and are still barred by Serb hardliners from returning to their homes.
"German authorities do not seem to pay attention to where these people come from," spokesman for the agency, Kris Janowski, told Reuters.
Aid officials have called the repatriation process premature at a time when nationalist authorities still enforce the country's division into ethnic communities.

Janowski said the deportation process was still not significant in numbers. "But the authorities are stepping the pace up and what is unfortunate is that you see more and more people deported from the category that we have asked to be still protected in Germany," he added.

Last year, Germany announced plans to send home 90,000 people by July 1 this year. In the first phase of the plan, single adults and childless couples were being targeted, with other refugees with children having to leave from May 1.
Financially burdened with more than 300,000 refugees from Bosnia it sheltered for five years, Germany took more people fleeing Yugoslavia's bloody breakup than any other West European country.
